Mallikarjun Sahukar, Aga) This Writ Petition Is Filed Under Articles 226 And 227 Of The Constitution Of India, Praying To Issue Writ Of Mandamus Directing The Respondent No.3 To Issue Registration Numbers To The Students From Serial No.1 To 39 Of The Petitioner'S College Who Are Studying In D-Pharma 1St Year For The Academic Year 2023-24 As Per Annexure-B By Considering The Representation Dated 09.09.2024 At Annexure-G, Writ Of Mandamus Directing The Respondent No.2 And 3 To Consider The Representation Dated 09.09.2024 And 03.01.2025 At Annexure-G And H. This Petition, Coming On For Order
texts.facts: However, there was a delay in submission of the necessary records regarding the students to respondent No.3 and also there was a delay in payment of necessary fee to the State. Consequently, the respondent No.3 has not granted the registration numbers to the students admitted by the petitioner-College. Hence, the petitioner-College made a representation to respondent No.3 to grant registration numbers to the students and permit them to appear in the examination. However, as the same was not considered, this writ petition has been filed with the The Cambridge College vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 30 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188485789/ 2
texts.arguments: In view of the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was always ready for verification of the documents of the students admitted for the year 2023-24 and in view of her submission that examinations to the D-Pharma first year is scheduled on 15.01.2025, respondent No.3 is directed to permit the students of the petitioner as mentioned in Annexure - B to the writ petition to face the examinations scheduled on 15.01.2025. Result of examinations shall however not be announced but is subject to the outcome of this petition. In the meanwhile, petitioner shall appear before respondent No.3 on 24.01.2025 for verification. During the course of the arguments the learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that though 40 students were admitted to the College, only 39 students submitted the necessary documents and the student at serial No.40 in Annexure-B to the writ petition did not do so. Hence, the prayer is limited to 39 students from serial Nos.1 to 39 in Annexure-B to the writ petition. 4. The learned Additional Government Advocate upon instructions submits that subsequent to filing of the writ petition, the details of the students have been verified and the students listed at Serial The Cambridge College vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 30 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188485789/ 3 Nos.1 to 39 are found NC: 2025:KHC-K:3498 HC-KAR eligible to be admitted to the course of D-Pharma. It is also submitted that the necessary fee has been paid by the College, though belatedly. 5. It is submitted by both the petitioner and respondents that subsequent to the interim orders of this Court, 39 students have been permitted to write the first year examination and their results are not announced as the writ petition is still pending. 6. Admittedly, petitioner-College has been accorded necessary permission to offer D-Pharma course. Petitioner-College has admitted students at serial Nos.1 to 39 as per Annexure-B to the writ petition for the academic year 2023-24.
